abstract: Recently, MPEG opens activity to standardize scene representation for lightweight application on mobile phone. The standard is named as LASeR, which is to improving and making efficient rich media application and services on mobile device. In this standard, a method for simple aggregation format (SAF) are provided, which is a streaming-ready format for packaging scenes and media together and streaming them onto such protocols as HTTP, TCP, MPEG-2, and so on. In this paper, we introduce SAF and show how different between a similar standard, MPEG-4 systems, and LASER.

articleTitle: An advanced receiver architecture for global terrestrial TV reception for automotive & mobile applications
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper presents a new innovative terrestrial hybrid TV receiver for automotive and multimedia application. The core of the concept is optimized for global digital and analog TV and radio transmission systems. A novel IF signal processing architecture with integrated selectivity by means of complex mixing, integrated Nyquist slope and tracking filters provides channel filtering, AGC and analog demodulation. The overall system performance will be demonstrated, the advantages of a universe, simplified application is illustrated.

articleTitle: A new spectral enhancement algorithm in MP3 audio
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper proposes a new blind method of spectral (high frequency) enhancement of MP3 audio. Due to the protocol constraint, the audio bandwidth of MP3 is restricted to 16 kHz at 128 kbps and 12 kHz at 64 kbps. Although band-restricted MP3 audio provides savings of storage space and network bandwidth, it suffers a major problem of a loss in high frequency fidelity such as localization, ambient information, and bright nature of audio. In contrast to previous works, this paper suggests a couple of new approaches such as dynamic cut-off finding, harmonic compensation and the gain-controlled high frequency compensation. Furthermore, the proposed algorithm requires less computational power with better high frequency enhancement capability compared to the previous works. The proposed algorithm is implemented on TI TMS6713 DSP platform and tested with IFP 800 model MP3 player. Audio quality of the proposed algorithm is reported and compared using spectrum analysis.

articleTitle: jGL ES - a J2ME-based 3D library for mobile devices
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: To provide 3D programs for all kinds of mobile devices, platform-dependent is still a big problem. In this paper, we present a platform-independent 3D graphics library, jGL ES, which is based on J2ME and has a similar programming environment as OpenGL ES. With jGL ES, the programmers can follow the same programming style of the framework of OpenGL ES and smoothly transfer their source codes to be cross-platform applications.

articleTitle: Optimized image formatting and display using active format description data (AFD)
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper describes work currently underway in the Consumer Electronics Association (CEA) to define recommended receiver response to active format description (AFD) data transported within the digital video signal. AFD may be utilized by receivers to automatically reformat digital displays for the optimum viewing experience, and to help avoid the all-too-familiar "postage stamp video" problem. The paper gives examples of some of the defined AFD states, and reviews the guiding principles behind development of the recommendation.

articleTitle: Throughput enhancement for uploading TCP flows in IEEE 802.11 wireless LAN
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper re-analyzes the relationship between MAC contention and TCP congestion control misled in previous efforts. By introducing a prioritized access of an access point, we seek to allow the optimal number of competing stations to contend for media access.

articleTitle: Power-aware rate-control for QoS provisioning over CDMA networks
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper presents a power-aware rate control method that dynamically adjusts the encoding bit rate according to the receiving power level of mobile stations (MSs) in CDMA network. The proposed rate-control method performs bit allocation at the video frame level using the estimated channel bit rate to minimize the average distortion over wireless video transmission. Experimental results show that the proposed method can significantly enhance the video quality in CDMA networks.

articleTitle: A new enhanced coding scheme for robust bit-stream of ATSC DTV
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: In this paper a new enhanced coding scheme of ATSC DTV standard is presented. The proposed coding scheme is a modified trellis codes of enhanced 8-VSB for robust bit-stream mode. By computing the distance spectrum, we derive the theoretical upper bound on the first event error probability of the proposed trellis codes. Based on the derivation, the proposed coding scheme has slightly better performance on AWGN channel than the conventional enhanced 8-VSB coding scheme at high signal-to-noise ratio (SNR). We also show that the proposed coding scheme has better performance than any existing coding schemes of ATSC DTV standard by using the Monte Carlo simulations.

articleTitle: Minimization of the PAPR of OFDM for wireless LAN
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper proposes a block code that minimizes the PAPR of OFDM for wireless LAN. Here, the code is implemented with a shift register and codeword inverter. Encoding of the code consists of searching a seed codeword, shifting the register elements and inverting the codeword. Since the OFDM system with the proposed code has the minimum PAPR, flexible design of a power amplifier at the transmitter end is possible.

articleTitle: AR-based indoor navigation system for personal locating
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper describes the personal location method in image sequences using a wearable computer for AR-based indoor navigation system which allows the user to navigate an unfamiliar and unknown place in an indoor environment. For identifying personal location in image sequences, the system uses a color histogram matching method. Personal locations recognized by the proposed method in real-time. The results are overplayed on the user's view through AR technique. The ideas presented in this system are applicable to a navigation system.

articleTitle: Copyright protection through feature-based watermarking using scale-invariant keypoints
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper presents a feature-based watermarking method based on scale-invariant keypoints for copyright protection. We extract feature points by using scale-invariant keypoint extractor and then these points are decomposed into a set of disjoint triangles. The triangles are watermarked by an additive way. Our method is compared with previous methods.

articleTitle: SoC design of an auto-focus driving image signal processor for mobile camera applications
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper presents a CMOS system on a chip (SoC) solution to capture focused images for mobile camera phones. In this work, auto focus (AF) lens has been formed by voice coil motor (VCM) type and the image signal processor (ISP) includes a built-in AF control block and AF driver to fully implement AF with fast and accurate performance. The proposed ISP with AF driver can meet constraints such as small size and low cost for mobile camera applications.

articleTitle: Visual video summaries post-processing using supervised and unsupervised classification
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Visual summaries allow users to grasp the overall content of a video, and access specific sequences within the video itself. The post-processing method presented in this paper makes it possible create exhaustive and not redundant visual video summaries. Three steps compose the method: the first removes the meaningless key frames; the second groups the key frames into clusters to allow multi-level summary presentation; and the third identifies the default summary level.

articleTitle: A novel digital audio processing scheme based on bit expansion asynchronous dithering
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper presents an asynchronous dithering scheme based on bit expansion subtractive dithering as well as bit expansion non subtractive dithering algorithm to enhance the quality of digital audio playback. The bit expansion asynchronous dithering system is suitable for implementation on both portable CD players and Hi-Fi systems with improved sound quality with enhanced performance in tone, smoothness and dynamic range. This scheme is particularly appealing to portable CD players due to its relatively low power requirement.

articleTitle: Optimal beam-selection algorithm for reception performance improvement of ATSC 8-VSB DTV
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper proposes an optimal beam-selection DTV receiver which uses switched beam-selection techniques. Usually the ATSC DTV receiver uses equalizer for compensating channel distortion. But multipath signals and Doppler effect easily affected performance of the receiver. A proposed optimal beam-selection DTV receiver reduces multipath signals so a burden of equalizer is reduced. Channel compensation is easier than a conventional DTV receiver which uses only equalizer. Simulation results show that performance of the proposed system is better than a conventional DTV receiver

articleTitle: Twin-cell detection for spread spectrum code in the presence of fractional Doppler frequency offset
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: In this paper, a novel detection method called the twin-cell detection is addressed for spread spectrum code acquisition in the presence of fractional Doppler frequency offset (FDFO). When the FDFO exists, the correlation peak used for detection during the acquisition process is split into two smaller neighboring peaks, resulting in severe degradation in the detection performance (and, consequently, in the overall acquisition performance). In the twin-cell detection, a decision variable for detection is formed by combining two consecutive correlator outputs, so that the reduction in the correlation value due to the FDFO can be alleviated. The simulation results show that the proposed scheme can offer better acquisition performance over the conventional scheme based on the cell-by-cell detection.

articleTitle: Browsing video recordings using movie-in-a-minute
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Having entered the terabyte consumer storage era and sailing towards petaand hexa- storage, we still have only adequate tools for browsing megabytes of stored video information. Movie-in-a-minute is a summarization method that generates a short video preview composed of automatically selected portions of a video recording. It aims at conveying key aspects of a program and its story in an efficient and entertaining manner. In doing so, movie-in-a-minute allows easy management of hundreds of hours of stored video programs. In this paper we present an approach to generate movie-in-a-minute previews based on automatic video and audio content analysis. The method has been formalized using a knowledge-explicit approach, implemented and tested as a new feature for consumer digital recorders.

articleTitle: Modeling and analysis for optimal PVR implementation
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper presents a methodology of analyzing the required elements to design an HD-PVR (high definition-personal video recorder) with efficient architecture. The bus modeling method is based on the RMS (rate monotonic scheduling) algorithm and provides a convenient way to predict the performance of the architecture of real-time systems and modify its architecture with optimal resources.

articleTitle: Frequency-domain equalization for distributed terrestrial DTV transmission environments
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper presents a frequency-domain direct-inversion equalization method for DTV receivers to deal with 0 dB ghosts. To secure the existence of a channel inverse, channel-matched filtering and noncausal filtering are performed prior to equalization. Simulation results show that the proposed method has a comparable performance to the ideal DFE

articleTitle: Two TV interfaces for accessing contents at ease in an "always-recording" multi-channel situation
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: We propose two TV interfaces for accessing a rich variety of contents stored in large-capacity HDD at ease. The first one is designed for handling multi-stream data received by multiple TV tuners and searching multiple TV channels simultaneously. The second one is deigned for handling a time range and searching for scenes in that range. These interfaces can be implemented on commercial products such as PCs, TVs and HDD recorders.

articleTitle: A smart model HD DVD/DVD/CD compatible pickup
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: We propose a compatible pickup for HD DVD/DVD/CD systems, which uses a blue/red/IR multi beam laser unit and a single sensor unit. The optical path of the DVD system is aligned to that of HD DVD system to share one sensor area. Experimental results confirm the practically of the proposed pickup

articleTitle: A H.264 video coprocessor for mobile DVB-H terminals
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: The new DVB-H standard allows broadcasting of audio/video content to mobile terminals. Such devices underlie severe restrictions concerning computational power and power consumption. The most computational intensive and therewith most power consuming part of such terminals is the decoding of the H.264/AVC video datastream. We present optimization strategies for software-based H.264/AVC video decoding as well as the architecture of a H.264/AVC decoding companion chip with specialized coprocessors, which target the above mentioned restrictions.

articleTitle: Adaptive write strategy selection mechanism for optical recording systems
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper discusses a smart algorithm for setting the write strategy in an optical recording device like consumer DVD recorders. The proposed algorithm improves the quality of recorded optical media, being particularly efficient for recordable and rewritable DVDs. One of the biggest challenges faced by optical recorder manufacturers is the increasing availability of low-cost optical media that obey marginally the standardized specifications causing poor recordability and corrupt discs. As the mass market embraces optical recorders in their homes, this problem aggravates resulting in consumer dissatisfaction. This paper presents a novel, yet not very complex method to improve the compatibility of conventional DVD recorders with widely available media.

articleTitle: Slim-type speaker for flat-panel televisions
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: An ultra-slim speaker incorporating a new sandwich-type magnetic circuit has been designed, making the speaker slimmer than a traditional one. The rigid diaphragm and the planar voice coil suppress the diaphragm's unwanted vibration mode and reproduces high quality sound. This slim speaker is suitable for flat-panel display televisions.

articleTitle: Adaptive group based intrablock refresh technique for MBMS systems
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Mobile phone besides being communication device is being transformed to another role as an entertainment device. Mobile devices enable the user to access entertainment such as TV anywhere and not limit it to just homes. It is expected that the traditional broadcast multimedia content is multicast instead of unicast to the mobile users to conserve bandwidth. 3GPP is currently working on a standard for multimedia broadcast and multicast services (MBMS). This paper presents an intra-refresh based error resilience technique for video delivery over MBMS. We propose an adaptive intra block refresh rate technique based on the loss statistics from the multicast group and dynamically partitioning multicast groups. The proposed technique improves average PSNR of the received video for all the multicast groups

articleTitle: Face transmission system for MPEG-4 mobile videophone via the wireless Internet
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: In this paper, we present an efficient face transmission system for MPEG-4 mobile videophone via the wireless Internet. The system consists of two stages: region segmentation and facial region detection. In the region segmentation, the input image is segmented into an appropriate set of arbitrary regions using a watershed algorithm. In facial region detection, the facial regions are identified from the segmented results using a skin-color model. The results of region segmentation and facial region detection are integrated to provide facial regions with accurate and closed boundaries. This system can be used to transmit a face to a corresponding person via the wireless Internet.

articleTitle: Complexity and memory reduction for high-quality interlace video coding in H.264/AVC
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: We propose two techniques for an H.264/AVC hardware encoder, maximum three reference fields selection and restriction of the number of MC size based on picture coding type. The proposed method can reduce complexity by more than 40% and the amount of memory by 25% without visual degradation.

articleTitle: An innovated DVD multi-angle content and a desired DVD player
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Although DVD specification introduced multi-angle video contents, until today, the multi-angle feature is not used much yet. This paper depicts an innovation of true user-interactive DVD multi-angle playback technology, and discusses the DVD player design to optimize the playback technology.

articleTitle: Realizing SMPTE-C standard colors on TV display with non-standard primaries
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: In this paper, a method is presented for realizing SMPTE-C standard colors on a TV display that does not have the standard primaries. Measurements of the color primary parameters of the display are obtained and used for transforming an input RGB signal to an output RGB signal, so that the perception of the output RGB signal on the display is same as the input RGB signal on a SMPTE-C standard display.

articleTitle: Hierarchically-paired evolutionary MAC protocol for ubiquitous wireless sensor applications
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: In this paper, we propose a new type of unified medium access control (MAC) framework, referred to as hierarchically-paired evolutionary MAC (HiPERMAC) protocol, with both contention-based and reservation-based time scheduling for wireless sensor networks. It is designed especially for a single-frequency radio operation while inheriting all advantages of the cluster-based hierarchical topology, e.g., energy efficiency and flexibility in coverage extension. Our simulation results show that depending on the various application scenarios, energy consumption and throughput can be properly traded off by our unified MAC framework.

articleTitle: A self-learning video-based face recognition system
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper presents a self-learning video-based face recognition system, which is targeted for the future intelligent home security or entertainment application. Unsupervised learning methods, temporal information, and the video context related logic rules are combined to keep the system running in an unsupervised way. Experiments demonstrate the robustness of the proposed prototype in unconstraint backgrounds.

articleTitle: Research and implementation on the mobile intelligent controller for consumer electronics
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper described the mobile intelligent controller providing an automatic home service based on a user's preference at a smart home. We presented the system architecture and the class diagram of mobile intelligent controller for consumer electronics. Also, we implemented ECG sensor, environment sensor and consumer electronics device driver for experiment. We applied different importance of contexts according to characteristics of consumer electronics. And we tested the performance of mobile intelligent controller for consumer electronics services. The testing result shows that the mobile intelligent controller predicts the service of consumer electronics effectively.

articleTitle: A novel system for remote control of household devices using digital IP phones
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: The idea of using a phone as a remote control for household devices is not new. However, new digital technologies such as voice-over-IP and signaling protocols such as SIP enable new methods of integrating the user interface of a phone with the digital IP infrastructure being deployed in the home. We developed and deployed the key press markup language and SIP event package (KPML) to address the need for a signaling-layer protocol for transmitting user stimulus from low-power, consumer devices such as IP phones to control household consumer devices.

articleTitle: Automatic selection of a visited network in mobile IPv6
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper describes an algorithm for automatic selection of a visited network in mobile IPv6 (MIPv6) such that the network selected is optimal with respect to MIPv6. As a result a seamless handover to a visited network is ensured and therefore continuously running applications like MP3 playback, a/V conferencing, IP telephony and multi-user gaming

articleTitle: An active entitlement key management for CA system on digital TV broadcasting system
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: In this paper, we propose an active entitlement key management scheme for CAS on digital TV broadcasting system. We introduce not only a novel concept of ARL for dynamic entitlement management, but also key distribution model based on four levels key hierarchy, and ARL transmission table for efficient transmission bandwidth consumption. With the proposed scheme, we can reduce key generation and encryption load considerably compared to passive entitlement management.

articleTitle: A robust two-antenna digital TV receiver for portable handsets with ultra-high interference cancellation
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper presents a robust two-antenna digital TV receiver optimized for portable handsets with ultra-high interference cancellation capability. An adaptive array direction control system drastically enhances desired OFDM signals, and it compensates undesired interference signals. An FPGA prototype of the Japanese ISDB-T 1-segment receiver demonstrates the improvement of D/U ratio by maximally 13 dB. Thus, any interference, e.g. analog TV signal, can be completely eliminated.

articleTitle: Two-stage false contour detection algorithm using re-quantization and directional contrast features and its application to adaptive false contour reduction
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper proposes a two-stage false contour detection algorithm using re-quantization and directional contrast features, with application to false contour reduction. In the first stage of false contour detection, smooth regions are first removed by bit-depth reduction and re-quantization. In the second stage, false contours are separated from edge or texture regions using directional contrast features, yielding the false contour detection map that shows possible candidate regions of false contours. For false contour reduction, adaptive directional smoothing filtering is applied only to candidate regions that are specified by the false contour detection map. Therefore the proposed algorithm is able to preserve sharp edges and details. Computer simulation with a large number of test images shows the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: A low cost algorithm for CFA data compression
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper introduces a new, low cost algorithm based on vector quantization (VQ) that allows compression of data in color filter array (CFA), the format provided by the physical sensor in almost all the digital still cameras (DSCs) and video cameras. The proposed method allows a compression of 45% with no visual loss in the output.

articleTitle: Multipurpose logo embedding method for copyright protection and authentication
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: In this paper, we propose a multipurpose logo embedding method by introducing the detection margin in the watermark detector. The innocent manipulations can be distinguished from malicious attacks by changing the detection margin. Simulation results show that the proposed algorithm is more robust than previously proposed algorithms and can detect malicious manipulations.

articleTitle: Motion estimation and mode decision for low power H.264
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper presents motion estimation and mode decision algorithms for low bit rate H.264, which reduces encoding complexity (by 70%) with little or no loss in visual quality.

articleTitle: Motion estimation and temporal up-conversion on the TM3270 media-processor
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: We present a qualitative performance evaluation of several components of a video format conversion algorithm (referred to as natural motion (NM)). The implementation platform is a new programmable media-processor, the TM3270, combined with dedicated hardware support. The performance of two compute-intense NM components, motion estimation (ME) and temporal up-conversion (TU), is evaluated. The impact of new TM3270 features, such as new video-processing operations and data prefetching, is quantified. We show that a real-time implementation of the ME and TU algorithms is achievable in a fraction of the available compute performance, when operating on standard definition video

articleTitle: An efficient algorithm for intra-prediction in H.264
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This work proposes a fast infra-prediction mode selection method for JVT video coding standard H.264. Based on the local edge information obtained by calculating edge feature parameters and sub-sampling of matching operations, the proposed method can reduced the encoding time about 26% considerably with less than 1.4% extra bits used and no more than 0.7 dB PSNR sacrificed

articleTitle: Home network remote controller using the appliance integrated script engine
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper presents a remote controller for home network systems that works on all network appliances. We discuss problems of home network systems which are composed of different types of sub-networks combined with bridges and gateways. Then we propose a solution to the problems using "appliance integrated script" (AIS) as common definition shared by all sub-networks and "AIS engine" to execute the script.

articleTitle: Adaptive format conversion of videos using wavelets
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: In this paper, we propose and implement adaptive schemes for video format conversions, involving spatial and temporal resolution changes. Individual adaptive schemes for spatial interpolation, deinterlacing and frame rate conversion (FRC) are proposed. The proposed method introduces adaptive schemes for all three video format conversion tasks, such that edges in the spatial and motion in the temporal domain is preserved. Using wavelet techniques, the best angle of interpolation is found so that interpolation is accomplished along the edges. Also, a second fold adaptation for interpolation is provided by frequency selective filters, whereby the interpolation filter is determined by the frequency characteristics of the local data. A scheme for accurate motion estimation for deinterlacing and motion vector estimation for high quality FRC using wavelets are developed. Extensive simulation performed on various images and videos shows the efficiency of the proposed method in comparison to other linear and non-linear methods in terms of objective and subjective measures.

articleTitle: Cluster based self-organization management protocols for wireless sensor networks
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This study proposes a scheme for self-organization management protocols of higher-level nodes to contest member nodes with multi-hop form hierarchical clusters, introduce the "20/80 rule" for determining the ratio of headers to member nodes, and develop a new cluster-based routing protocol that integrates the inter-cluster on-demand routing and the intra-cluster table-driven routing applied in the sensor networks for further consumer applications.

articleTitle: Advanced conditional access system for digital broadcasting receivers using metadata
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: We propose an advanced conditional access system (CAS) for digital broadcasting receivers using program related information, called metadata. The proposed advanced CAS provides a secure system for content and metadata on digital broadcasting receivers, by preventing tampering and ensuring that only metadata certified by the broadcaster can be utilized.

articleTitle: Protection of MPEG-2 multicast streaming in IP-TV
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper presents a protection of broadcasting service using MPEG-2 multicast streaming in environment of IP based set-top box (STB). This protection scheme is free of key synchronization problem of digital rights management (DRM) system and more efficient than condition access system (CAS) in bandwidth respect.

articleTitle: AFORE: an IFFT/FFT core generation tool different wireless communication standards
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: In this paper, we propose a software tool that generates single or multiple mode IFFT/FFT cores. This tool can be configured for different wireless communication standards that use OFDM modulation such as WLAN 802.11a/g, WMAN 802.16a, DAB, DVB-T. The resulting FFT/IFFT core fulfills the timing specifications of each standard with a minimum area.

articleTitle: Architecture for video summarization services over home networks and the Internet
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: With increasing number of personal digital video recorders, the idea of having summarization functionality to view the recorded content has also been gaining importance. The summarization functionality can either be built into the video recording device or can reside in a computing device on the network. In this paper, we present a client-server architecture for the latter case. Then, we present two possible application scenarios that the proposed architecture can enable. The first application is to enable summarization services over a home network. The second application is to enable summarization services over the Internet.

articleTitle: A channel estimation method based on pilot and EM algorithm for OFDM systems
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: A channel estimation method based on pilot and EM algorithm is proposed. The channels are estimated using the EM (expectation-maximization) algorithm, while making use of pilot tones to obtain the initial estimate for iterative steps. Simulation results show that the bit error rate (BER) can be significantly reduced compared with conventional algorithm and iterative times are less than the common EM algorithm. A VLSI architecture for the algorithm is proposed

articleTitle: An automatic analyzer for sports video databases using visual cues and real-world modeling
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: With the advent of hard-disk video recording, video databases gradually emerge for consumer applications. The large capacity of disks requires the need for fast storage and retrieval functions. We propose a semantic analyzer for sports video, which is able to automatically extract and analyze key events, such as player behavior. The analyzer employs several visual cues and a model for real-world coordinates, so that speed and position of a player can be determined with sufficient accuracy. It consists of four processing steps: (1) playing event detection, (2) court and player segmentation, as well as a 3-D camera model, (3) player tracking, and (4) event-based high-level analysis exploiting visual cues extracted in the real-world. We show attractive experimental results remarking the system efficiency and classification skills.

articleTitle: DVB-H for wireless broadband terminal access - a performance evaluation
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: The DVB-H (digital video broadcasting handheld) technology fosters mobile connectivity of handheld and in-vehicle terminals. This paper presents a performance analysis of the DVB-H standard. The focus is on the performance of the broadcast link to a terminal equipped with a small built-in antenna. The analysis was carried out for a large variety of usage scenarios and the corresponding channel characteristics

articleTitle: R-D optimized frame-skipping transcoder for low bit rate video transmission
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: We propose a new real-time rate-distortion (R-D) optimized dynamic frame-skipping (DFS) transcoder for low bit rate video transmission. The proposed transcoder can adjust the number of skipped frames according to the target frame rate as well as the channel rate. Experimental results indicate that the proposed R-D optimized transcoder can not only perform frame-skipping effectively but also improve visual quality in the low bit rate video transcoding.

articleTitle: In-camera person-indexing of digital images
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: A prototype implementation of an automatic in-camera cataloging tool is presented. An external infrastructure to store and analyze images and support the in-camera cataloging tool is also described.

articleTitle: A roadscape analysis system of vehicle mounted camera-image
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: A roadscape analysis system was developed that can analyze images captured by a camera mounted on a vehicle. The system divides images into cells, calculates five features of each cell, and distinguishes between "town," "forest," and "plain" automatically.

articleTitle: Real-time carousel caching and monitoring in data broadcasting
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper proposes a digital storage media command and control (DSM-CC) carousel caching and management architecture that can support priority-based scheduling of monitoring threads and the caching mechanism of carousel objects for a quick launch and download of Xlet. This proposed architecture is able to accommodate the data broadcasting middleware that uses DSM-CC object carousel mechanisms, such as advanced common application platform (ACAP), open cable application platform (OCAP), and multimedia home platform (MHP).

articleTitle: Investigation and complexity analysis of a spatial audio codec based on a programmable media-processor
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper presents a complexity analysis of a spatial audio coding scheme (known as MPEG surrounding) based on a commercially available programmable device. The analysis mainly focuses on the complexity of spatial audio cue analysis and synthesis, especially for the additional special tools used during the spatial cue synthesis stage. The analysis results can be a reference during building up a SAC codec on a DSP

articleTitle: A study on selection of video levels compromising dynamic false contour and gray scale rendition in PDP
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Effective error measures are proposed to quantify false contours and error diffusion noise. By considering the trend of the errors, a method is presented that selects the proper number video levels compromising two conflicting issues of dynamic false contour (DFC) problem and gray scale rendition (GSR).

articleTitle: DSP implementation of the 3GPP enhanced aacPlus decoder
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper presents implementation of the 3GPP (the 3rd generation partnership project) enhanced aacPlus decoder on a 16-bit fixed-point DSP. Enhanced aacPlus is a 3GPP standard integrating newly standardized MPEG-4 parametric stereo (PS) into MPEG-4 high efficiency advanced audio coding (HE-AAC). PS enables audio coding at a low bitrate for stereo signals by efficiently representing stereo information. The maximum number of operations for the implemented decoder is 29.3 million cycles per second for a 32 kb/s bitstream. This implementation with stereo decoding capability achieves higher sound quality than mono HE-AAC at the cost of 90% increase in computational complexity. 3GPP mobile terminals for music download and streaming services can be realized by using the implemented decoder.

articleTitle: Spatio-temporal filter with adaptive multiple outliers rejector
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Digital images captured in dim light conditions can be very noisy: mixtures of different noise types may damage the image signal, e.g. impulsive and Gaussian noises. A spatio-temporal filter is proposed, which is capable to eliminate multiple adjacent defective pixels and reduce Gaussian noise in the raw data acquired by the image sensor. The proposed solution is adaptive in that it automatically adjusts its sensitivity, depending on the estimated noise.

articleTitle: Location based service based on digital multimedia broadcasting
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper presents a new location based service (LBS) that can be provided in digital multimedia broadcasting (DMB) transmission system economically and effectively. We propose a point of interest (POI) protocol compatible to transport protocol experts group (TPEG) and introduce the POI data server and the verification platform implemented by using the proposed protocol. As a filed result, the stability and effectiveness of proposed protocol is verified.

articleTitle: New channel estimation scheme exploiting decision feedback symbols for OFDM systems
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: The conventional pilot-aided channel estimation schemes use the fixed number of pilots to estimate the channel. In this paper, the channel estimator exploits reliable decision feedback symbols as quasi-pilots. This new channel estimation scheme is commercially attractive without additional hardware in the receiver using DSP chips for the OFDM systems.

articleTitle: Edge-preserving spatial deinterlacing for still images using block-based region classification
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: A number of deinterlacing algorithms have been proposed, however, they have some drawbacks: blocking artifacts or blurring around edges. To overcome these drawbacks, we propose an edge-preserving spatial deinterlacing algorithm using block-based region classification. The proposed algorithm classifies blocks of a line into three types of regions: connected, shaded, and unshaded. It finds the best matched block and interpolates lines block by block. Experimental results give better performance than conventional spatial deinterlacing algorithms, especially near edges, in terms of the peak signal to noise ratio (PSNR) and subjective visual quality.

articleTitle: Implementation of RAMO-based Multimedia Applications on MPEG-4 Platform
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper reports the implementation of the concepts of the reactive and adaptive multimedia object model (RAMO) via a guided review of its development process on a MPEG-4 rendering platform. The implementation of a simple iTV application is presented as well as a content animation engine. These activities have been achieved in the context of the ITEA Jules Verne project

articleTitle: Ensuring coexistence for high-speed powerline carrier applications
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This document describes typical use cases for home networks and access networks, primarily from the consumer electronics industry's point of view. From these use cases, market requirements are derived for a powerline carrier (PLC) network to satisfy the use cases. Upon reviewing the uses cases and market requirements derived from those use cases, it becomes clear that two or more PLC technologies will be required in a home to efficiently satisfy these requirements. Furthermore, it becomes self-evident that at least two technologies would be typical in an apartment building, where many homes share the same low-voltage wiring. Thus, one requirement for any PLC technology becomes its coexistence with other technologies on the same line. The paper details this particular requirement, defining the coexistence mechanism necessary to fulfil the use cases and efficiently meet all the market requirements. This paper was written by the Technical Working Group of Consumer Electronics Powerline Communications Alliance (CEPCA). Contributions to this paper came primarily from seven companies; Hitachi, Mitsubishi, Panasonic, Pioneer, Toshiba, Sony, and Yamaha.

articleTitle: User-centric and remote content browsing for mobile devices
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: In this paper, we propose a provision of user-centric mobile media album system and albuming functions to support it. For the system, we are considering both a stand-alone type implementation and a PC bundle type implementation. The main idea of the user-centric and remote content browsing for albuming functions is to enable users to organize and browse their photos along the semantically meaningful axes that are event, person-identity, and category while the highlights of video contents are processed by PC and easily downloaded and watched on mobile devices. Experiment results demonstrate that the proposed method would be useful to browse photos and video clips.

articleTitle: Real-time detecting system of the driver's fatigue
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper presents a real-time detecting system based on the DSP processor. It uses real-time operating system DSP/BIOS to build tasks and interruptions, and will give out an incurrence of phonetic warning when the driver is tired

articleTitle: Digital television receivers with blind iterative linear cancellers
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Conventional equalization algorithms have been used with limited success in multipath mitigation for 8-VSB reception. This paper presents a modified iterative linear canceller (ILC) with blind startup optimized for 8-VSB application. Simulation results demonstrating superiority of the new scheme to existing methods and near multipath-free performance is presented.

articleTitle: A highly efficient blind carrier frequency estimator for wireless OFDM systems
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper presents a highly efficient blind estimator for carrier frequency offsets that are much larger than the subcarrier spacing in orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) systems. The proposed scheme is shown to have a high accuracy and an acquisition range that spans the entire OFDM spectrum. The system performance is assessed over frequency-selective fading channels.

articleTitle: Secure remote USIM (universal subscriber identity module) card application management protocol for W-CDMA networks
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Even though 3GPP presents a secure remote card application protocol through W-CDMA networks, it is unstable in terms of security and key management. For solving the weakness of 3GPP, we propose a WPKI (WAP public key infrastructure) based secure remote USIM (universal subscriber identity module) card application management protocol, which is used in W-CDMA networks.

articleTitle: Revocation in the video content protection system
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: VCPS (video copy protection system) protects broadcast flag and copy-once content on DVD+R/+RW (digital versatile disc + recordable/rewritable) media. It provides device revocation using a key block on the media. Based on a statistical model, we analyze the dynamics of the key block size.

articleTitle: Software-configurable adaptive array antenna system for ISDB-T reception
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper presents an adaptive array antenna system for ISDB-T reception (Japan digital TV broadcasting) with the adaptive array algorithm is configurable by software. By exploiting the merits of software-defined radio (SDR), a number of adaptive algorithms such as digital beamforming and/or null-steering (i.e. maximum ratio combining - MRC, sample matrix inversion SMI) are embedded in DSP board that is reconfigurable according to the radio propagation environment. The experiment results for MRC and SMI algorithms successfully improved BER performance for ISDB-T reception with an analog TV interference and intersymbol interference by over GI delay waves.

articleTitle: A low-complexity FEC assignment scheme for motion JPEG2000 over wireless network
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: In this paper, a heuristic FEC assignment schemes for unequal error protection of motion JPEG2000 streams is proposed, which uses the slope of the rate-distortion curve to choose the code for each quality layer. Simulation results proved that it can attain better quality and lower complexity compared to conventional FEC assignment methods.

articleTitle: Dual-channel video-graphics-controller for HDTV flat-panel display TV
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper presents a high integrated high-performance video processing system-on-chip for HDTV displays. The IC unites the complete processing chain for dual-channel display and can be directly connected to a PDP or LCD by LVDS or RGB resp. It comprises a 3D-comb filter, two color-decoders, two channel motion adaptive de-interlacer with a new algorithm to eliminate staircase effects, as well as scaling, picture-improvement and frame-rate conversion processing units. A powerful 32 bit CPU controls internal and external tasks and a high-resolution pixel-graphic is generated for on-screen menus and teletext display

articleTitle: USB-based home control system using OSGi
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper presents the design of a USB home controller and a home control system that specially is focused on controlling home appliances as a part of home network systems, the implementation of the USB device access class in an OSGi service platform and a home security system as an application.

articleTitle: Improving detection performance of pre-coded STBC OFDM by re-generating pre-coded symbols
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: The pre-coded STBC transmission is an effective scheme in order to improve performance of OFDM under frequency selective fading channels. However, its performance degrades very severe frequency selective fading. In this paper, an iterative detection scheme of the pre-coded STBC OFDM scheme is proposed and good performance is confirmed by computer simulation.

articleTitle: Multimedia digital rights management using modified motion vector for mobile device
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper presents a new digital rights management (DRM) that modifies the motion vector (MV) of macroblock (MB) for mobile device. Experimental results indicate that the proposed DRM can not only achieve very low cost of the encryption but also enable separable authentication to individual mobile devices such as portable multimedia player (PMP) and personal digital assistants (PDA).

articleTitle: Performance evaluation of an ICI self-cancellation coded digital video broadcasting transceiver
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Digital video broadcasting-terrestrial (DVB-T) is an important multimedia technology capable of high data-rate transmission. Orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) is the backbone technique in the current DVB-T systems adopted by Europe and Japan. However, the OFDM system is very sensitive to the intercarrier interference (ICI) induced by the Doppler frequency drift and the fading channels. A means to deal with the ICI problem is called the ICI self-cancellation or polynomial cancellation coding scheme. In this paper, we evaluate the effectiveness of the ICI self-cancellation coded DVB-T system compared with the existing DVB-T system using the convolutional coding for different fading channels.

articleTitle: Intelligence service binding architecture for interoperability between home network devices
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Existing home devices in home network provides only independent service and doesn't fully support a intelligent service provided by intercommunicating among devices. In this paper, we suggest the intelligent service binding architecture which is allow users to figure out the status of devices and to interlock among home devices.

articleTitle: A method of accurate DTV transport streams splicing
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Because of the difference of decoding and displaying order, special process is required for frame unit based DTV transport splicing. This paper proposed an accurate TS splicing method. This method applies video transcoding techniques to change picture coding type and bitrate, so that TS can be spliced accurately. In addition, TS multiplex strategy is also used to guarantee no STD buffer overflow occurs.

articleTitle: Audio/video processing for single-chip T-DMB decoder
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper deals with aspects of audio/video processing for the T-DMB decoder chips. The proposed architectures were implemented in a new T-DMB decoder SoC. This SoC comprises all units required for T-DMB multimedia decoding such as system demultiplexer, MPEG-4 AVC/H.264 video decoder and MPEG-4 BSAC audio decoder. The proposed audio/video decoder has low power consumption and has been implemented using a standard-cell library in 0.18 /spl mu/m 1P6M CMOS technology.

articleTitle: Reliable right management scheme in cable home network
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper presents a right management scheme in cable home network using cable modem with home gateway. The proposed scheme provides the control of right management via conditional access system from head-end of cable operator, as well as greater control flexibility of stored contents on digital video recorder to authorized devices in cable home network.

articleTitle: Using divide-and-conquer on custom lengthened Fourier transforms
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Fourier transforms (FTs) are the key to all modern, OFDM-based (orthogonal frequency division multiplexing) transmission schemes. This paper demonstrates the principles and the efficient implementation of arbitrary length FTs, using divide and conquer techniques for decomposition into "atomic" transforms. Using "digital radio mondiale" as an example, we present generalized FT processing hardware, its complexity, processing time, precision and design re-use.

articleTitle: The v2.0+EDR Bluetooth SOC architecture for multimedia
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper proposes the advanced Bluetooth SOC architecture for multimedia applications. Our design includes baseband functions in compliance with Bluetooth core specification v2.0+EDR (enhanced data rate), RF transceiver, modem, SBC codec, ESIC processor, and power management block. This chip is SIP integration with the flash memory and occupies a die size of 28 mm/sup 2/ in CMOS 0.18 /spl mu/m. The maximum current consumption of the total chip is 65 mA. The single operation voltage of the analog and the digital parts is 1.8 V.

articleTitle: Profile face detection using block difference feature for automatic image annotation
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: We propose a new profile face detection system for automatic image annotation. For personal images, profile face detection is required because faces turn in different directions. To reduce the numerous false detections seen in previous approaches, we propose a block difference feature. The experiments we describe show the successful outcome of this strategy.

articleTitle: Efficient SVC encoding scheme for the video transmission over various networks
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: In this paper, we propose an efficient encoding scheme in scalable video coding (SVC) for the video transmission over various networks. In order to improve the encoding efficiency, we adopt the spatio-temporal motion vector (MV) prediction method in the motion compensated temporal filtering (MCTF). Experimental results show that the proposed method outperforms the conventional method in terms of compression ratio.

articleTitle: High-sensitivity and high-mobility compact DVB-T receiver for in-car entertainment
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: A compact DVB-T receiver with better than -94 dBm sensitivity for in-car usage is presented. Dual tuners are included in the receiver to reduce multi-path effects as well as realize the diversity technique. A robust audio/video interface (AVIO) is defined to accommodate different kinds of in-car displays with a variety of A/V specs. In addition, a protection circuit is proposed to provide the convenience that either active antennas or passive antennas can be plugged in the same antenna sockets. Field trials proved that the receiver works perfectly when the car is running over 180 Km/hr.

articleTitle: Masking coding artifacts on large displays
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: To improve the picture quality on high-end display systems, coding artifact reduction is an important function in the video processing chain. We investigate the use of a masking algorithm to reduce the visibility of coding artifacts that typically result from lossy, block-based compression methods.

articleTitle: Seamless QoS adaptation control for embedded multimedia communications
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper proposes a seamless QoS adaptation control (SQAC) for embedded multimedia communications. The fundamental control procedure of SQAC accounts for the limited computational capability and memory of the embedded system, and the MPEG-4 object priority. SQAC supports adaptation control and offers seamless steady multimedia streaming based on monitoring mobile network traffic and the computing resources of the client, including the status of the CPU and the memory. When the available resources are not enough, the client releases some unnecessary system processes to obtain more available memory and CPU computing resources for application. A priority-based differentiated presentation control mechanism is proposed to balance the workload of the embedded system based on medium object priority

articleTitle: An implementation of FTTH based home gateway supporting various services
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: HG (home gateway) is an interface device that connects an access network, WAN (wide area network), to a home network. FTTH (fiber to the home) based HG is an HG with FTTH network as an access network interface. In this paper, we propose an implementation of FTTH based HG, specially EPON (Ethernet passive optical network) based HG. With the FTTH access network interface, the proposed HG can provide service bandwidth of 100 Mbps to 1 Gbps to each subscriber. The amount is enough bandwidth to provide various home network services for each one. Our proposed HG has a novel architecture with various home network interfaces and can use efficiently the abundant bandwidth for the various services.

articleTitle: Analysis of listeners' favorite music by music features
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: The relationship between listeners' favorite music and the music features was analyzed. Music was classified on the basis of a rating system performed by listeners, and the music features were analyzed. The analysis showed that the listeners' favorite music tended to concentrate along certain music feature axes. In addition, the concentrated music feature axis varies with the pairs of listeners and artists.

articleTitle: Context-based video browsing interface for PVR-enabled high-definition television systems
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: We describe an implementation of our previously developed temporal-context-based video browsing interface, on a PVR-enabled high-definition television system. The implementation poses significant challenges such as consuming minimal computational resources so as to avoid disrupting any of the existing functionalities, sampling the stored video frames using a 1394 AV/C connection, and rendering the sampled images in a visually pleasing and useful way. Our implementation successfully addresses the aforementioned challenges by taking advantage of the target platform's facilities for high-quality video scaling and frame sampling.

articleTitle: A novel low supply voltage VCO for IEEE 802.11a W-LAN
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: In this paper we present a 1-V low supply voltage CMOS VCO; it not only can increase the turning range of the VCO but also can decrease the phase noise. The proposed VCO achieves a phase noise of -116.73 dBc/Hz at the offset frequency of 1 MHz, respectively. The tuning range of 1 GHz is achieved with the control voltage from 0.25 V to 0.85 V. It can also be used in the receiver for the IEEE 802.11a.

articleTitle: Efficient audio/video synchronization method for video telephony system in consumer cellular phones
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper presents an efficient audio/video synchronization method that is quite suitable for video telephony. In terms of computational complexity and simplicity of the software structure, the proposed algorithm shows improved results compared to the conventional synchronization algorithm. The derived audio/video synchronization algorithm is compactly expressed in a single decision rule. After simulations with real video telephony system based on Texas Instruments OMAP processor and Nucleus PLUS RTOS, we found the devised algorithm is quite suitable for consumer cellular phones with limited computational resources

articleTitle: AVATAR: an improved solution for personalized TV based on semantic interface
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: The search engines in Internet and the recommender systems in the digital TV domain, pursue to light the burden of users with access to massive amounts of information, by offering only data (and TV programs) of interest for them. In this paper, we emphasize the advantages of using the so-called semantic Web technologies in the development of an intelligent TV assistant, named AVATAR. Its main advantage is a great improvement with respect to previous TV recommenders, obtained by combining two personalization strategies with a novel common nexus related to semantic inference capabilities. By the inference, AVATAR discovers appealing and complex semantic associations between the user preferences and the finally recommended TV shows. It is worth noting that this inference process overcomes a drawback identified in the existing tools, which suggest programs too similar to those the user watched in the past. In this regard, our inference strategy provides the viewers with suggestions clearly enhanced, diversified and permanently updated to their personal preferences.

articleTitle: Carrier phase independent timing recovery methods for VSB receivers
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper proposes an alternative timing recovery method for VSB receivers. It employs a timing error detector which uses both in-phase and quadrature-phase component of received VSB signal and operates at twice of a symbol frequency. The proposed method shows the insensitivity to residual carrier phase offset contained in the signal, thus providing consistent performances regardless of carrier recovery status.

articleTitle: Accelerating speech coding standards through SystemC- synthesized SIMD and scalar accelerators
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: We developed parametric data-parallel and scalar instruction set extensions for accelerating the ITU-T G.723.1 and G.729.A speech coding standards. Using a novel hybrid methodology, we synthesized the custom hardware accelerators via encapsulating the C-based descriptions of the original scalar and SIMD instruction set extensions in a hybrid, SystemC- RTL hardware wrapper and introduced it into the scalar and vector extension datapaths of a next-generation configurable, extensible multi-threaded CPU. We discuss this methodology and present a VLSI implementation of a 128-bit wide configuration of the data-parallel and scalar coprocessor attached to a dual-threaded instance of this CPU.

articleTitle: A novel CMOS imager with 2-dimensional binarization and edge detection for highly integrated imaging systems
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: The proposed CMOS imager successfully embeds an advanced local threshold algorithm to simultaneously achieve the 2-dimensional operations of binarization and edge detection. Both functions provide a lot of widely spread applications for real-time imaging systems. A 64 /spl times/ 64 pixel array imager is implemented in the TSMC 0.35 /spl mu/m 2P4M technology. Each pixel has the size of 10 /spl mu/m /spl times/ 10 /spl mu/m with a fill factor of 36.1%. The test chip occupies 1.80 mm /spl times/ 1.63 mm and consumes 15 mW from a 3.3 V power supply.

articleTitle: Symbol overlapped multiwavelet packets based OFDM
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: A novel OFDM scheme based on the orthogonal multiwavelet packets and symbols overlapped scheme are proposed in the paper. Analysis result shows that the spectral efficiency can be improved by twofold compared to that of the conventional OFDM.

articleTitle: Evaluation of a hands-free unit during double-talk
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: The double-talk performance of a hands-free speech communication system is crucial to the overall quality. This paper presents a method to evaluate double-talk performance of conference phones and speakerphones. The method measures loudness, clipping and the amount of echo during double-talk.

articleTitle: Maximum ratio combining for OFDM systems with cochannel interference
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: In this paper, we investigate a receive diversity combining scheme for OFDM wireless LAN systems with cochannel interference. The scheme utilizes signal to interference plus noise power ratio (SINR) to obtain the weighting factors in maximal ratio combining. To estimate SINR, we use the coherency between the subchannels, which is caused by the limited delay spread of the multipath channel.

articleTitle: A report on field test results of enhanced VSB system
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: We provide field test results of enhanced VSB (E-VSB). In order to verify performance of the system, we measured E-VSB and 8-VSB signals in outdoor and indoor condition, and compare the results. The test results show that E-VSB signal is fully backward compatible with 8-VSB receiver and E-VSB has good reception performance in indoor condition.

articleTitle: Computer simulation system for three-dimensional speckle-shift hologram's recording
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: In this paper, we present an investigation about the 3D speckle-shift hologram, which is expected as a mass optical memory. First, we established three-dimensional computer simulation of the optical system. Using this system, the characteristic features of the recording method and multiplex methods for a hologram memory can be investigated.

articleTitle: Data hiding method for broadcasting system
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: A novel method of hiding data into multimedia contents by using watermarking technology is described in this paper. This method can be used for analog images, digital raw images, JPEG and other compressed images and has advantages over the existing data hiding methods in terms of less distortion to original multimedia contents, robustness against noise attacks, and efficient data embedding/detection. By modifying the summed value of selected DCT coefficients and making the quantization adaptive to the DCT amplitudes and other parameters, the data hiding method is found to be robust against signal distortions in broadcasting system due to noise, contrast and luminance change, pixel shift, and multi-path interference.

articleTitle: Wide band 3D Y/C separation circuit for PAL system with reduced memory size
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper reports newly developed 3D Y/C separation circuit of PAL system, which has been realized with a minimum frame memory structure, the same as that of an NTSC system, and has no deterioration of high-frequency components.

articleTitle: Robust decision-feedback equalization with a noncausal filter for ATSC DTV receivers
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper presents a robust decision-feedback equalization method for 8-VSB DTV receivers under severe channel environments where a 0-dB ghost exists. Noncausal filtering is employed to make a severe channel be mild. Simulation results show that the proposed method has more stable convergence than existing decision-feedback equalization schemes.

articleTitle: End-to-end approach to the development of powerline communication technologies
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper examines the pros and cons of methods for implementing powerline communications technologies for the digital home ecosystem. The methods presented herein emphasize the importance of international interoperable standards for all forms of powerline communication.

articleTitle: High frequency band dispersed tone line communication modem for networked appliances
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Power line communication modem for networked appliances was developed. To realize robust communication by reducing inference from noise and channel distortion, the PLC modem utilizes high frequency band for data transmission. Performance of communication and compatibility with radio communication were evaluated.

articleTitle: Implementation of synchronization for 2/spl times/2 MIMO WLAN systems
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: The proposed synchronization is designed for 2/spl times/2 MIMO OFDM WLAN systems. A novel CSIO structure is implemented to recover the carry frequency. The proposed design chiefly improves the conventional CORDIC-based structure which is used at each accumulated phase. Considering the iterative CORDIC computation, our CSIO structure only operates the CORDIC once. Moreover, the timing controller negotiates these two antenna input signals and gates the useless signal to reduce the power consumption. This architecture is simulated by UMC 0.18 /spl mu/m IP6M CMOS technology, and the CSIO function is also emulated by VirtexII XC2V1500. It provides the high precision with the area of 1.682 mm/sub 2/. The power consumption is 90.53 mW at 20 MHz.

articleTitle: An interface for multiple agents on shared 3D display
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: We describe a method to integrate user interfaces for interactions among users wear VR devices on wide stereoscopic display. The key technologies include the coordination with various 3D devices, game metaphor to share participant's intents, and seamless rendering of multiple channels to support real-time interactions.

articleTitle: Security camera system using sharply outlined display algorithm and variable-clock CVBS encoder
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: In this paper, we propose the security camera system that displays a sharp and clear image by using sharply outlined display algorithm and has less hardware complexity by using a modified composite video baseband signal generator of a variable-clock video encoder. The proposed system is fabricated with the test camera chip that has been manufactured by the MagnaChip 0.25 /spl mu/m CMOS process.

articleTitle: Sparse equalizer using adaptive weight activation for fast start-up in ATSC DTV systems
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: A sparse equalizer using a data-recycling algorithm is proposed for 8-vestigial sideband (VSB) digital television (DTV) equalizers. The proposed sparse equalizer with the data-recycling algorithm selects effective equalizer taps for channel equalization, thereby improving the convergence speed and output signal-to-noise ratio (SNR). The output SNR, convergence speed, and number of required equalizer taps are compared between the proposed and conventional algorithms in Brazilian channels and a single ghost dynamic channel.

articleTitle: Content distribution system based on MPEG-4 ISMACryp in set-top box environments
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: We implement ISMACryp-based digital content playing software and apply it to a commercial embedded Linux set-top box for enabling secure contents distribution system

articleTitle: Thread-parallel MPEG-4 and H.264 coders for system-on-chip multi-processor architectures
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: MPEG-4 and H.264 are rapidly becoming the most popular video coding algorithms for consumer devices. However, this is achieved at the expense of a computationally intensive encoding process and associated power consumption which currently limits their full deployment in portable, cost-sensitive consumer devices. We address the severe performance issue by exploiting thread-level parallelism to share the computational load between multiple processors in a system-on-chip multi-processor configuration. This can lead to significant power savings due to the lower frequency each processor is required to run. For MPEG-4, our custom multi-processor simulator delivers a reduction of 80% to 90% in dynamic instruction count per processor, at 22 processor contexts; for H.264 the theoretical reduction is a near-linear 25 % for four processor contexts, demonstrating a highly balanced multi-threaded implementation

articleTitle: Network AV streaming transmission technology
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper presents an original stable AV streaming technology via the Internet on digital TV (DTV) at low cost. Correcting lost packets on transmission path, image is reproduced stably. We have developed a prototype for DTV to support streaming technology. The prototype accepts digital broadcasting, Internet and home network.

articleTitle: Evaluation of a prototype remote control for digital broadcasting receivers by using semantic differential method
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: We prototyped an easy-to-use remote control for digital broadcasting receivers based on the result of usability tests that we made. In order to evaluate the prototype remote, we conducted experiments by using the semantic differential method. Two major components - "functionality" and "appearance" were extracted from the results of the principal component analysis. We found that there were significant differences in the each component score between the prototype remote control and a conventional one that had many buttons. The results indicate the effectiveness of our design methodology to develop an easy-to-use user interface.

articleTitle: HD DVD video player
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
