abstract: The new HD DVD-video player, specified from the DVD forum, has a new comprehensive software architecture that introduces a new interactive navigation system while still allowing the legacy DVD navigating system. This new software architecture allows for synchronization of picture in picture, HD graphics, menus, games, streaming network multimedia and HD video. The new HD DVD players includes network connectivity and persistent storage that allows a user to play network synchronized games, dynamically download new HD theater trailers and to save those trailers, game scores and other personalized information to internal persistent storage

articleTitle: A brightness adjustment method for MPEG-2 compressed video editing
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: A brightness adjustment special effects editing method in MPEG-2 compressed domain is proposed. The method is realized in the DCT domain of YUV color space without full frame decompression. Experimental results show that the visual quality of the edited video in the compressed domain is identical to the one edited in the uncompressed domain.

articleTitle: A lightweight and secure wireless certificate management protocol supporting mobile phone
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: In this paper, we propose a lightweight and secure wireless certificate management protocol that is applicable to the wireless Internet that has a constrained communication environment and the mobile phone that has fundamental limitation of performance, and show the implementation results of the scheme based on the mobile phone.

articleTitle: MPEG-7 over MPEG-4 systems decoder for using metadata
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: In this paper, we propose the MPEG-7 over MPEG-4 systems decoder, which is compatible with MPEG-4 systems specification and added MPEG-7 module, which uses OCI and MPEG-7 textual descriptor for content search, and it is provides content management and metadata information.

articleTitle: New architecture supporting plug and play of service for a home network system with flexible expandability
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: We propose a new architecture that supports the plug and play of service modules for a centrally managed home network system. Service modules are designed independent of the server package and are managed flexibly. Modules belonging to the same service class can be configured to work exclusively or cooperatively. This architecture provides the possibility to set up a system adapted to user needs, which contributes to the spread of home networks and further progress in consumer electronics.

articleTitle: An XML-based automated authentication profile for home network based on OSGi (open service gateway initiative) framework
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper proposes a single sign-on scheme in which a user offers his credential information to a home network working with the OSGi (open service gateway initiative) service platform for obtaining user authentication and controlling a remote device through a mobile device using this authentication scheme, based on SAML (security assertion markup language). Especially by defining the single sign-on profile, we provide a clue to applying automated user authentication to control a remote device for distributed mobile environments such as a home network based on OSGi.

articleTitle: Adaptive beam steering reception system for ISDB-T based on pre-FFT diversity technique
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Generally speaking, the reception of high bit rate transmissions such as high definition television (HDTV) in automobiles is poor. In this study, we developed an adaptive beam steering reception system and experimentally investigated the performance of this new system on a mobile terminal for HDTV reception. The experimental results show that the reception quality was significantly improved by the new system. It was found that by using the adaptive beam steering technique we can expect good performance of HDTV reception on an automobile across a larger area.

articleTitle: Design of a quiet-comfort headboard
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper presents the design of quiet-comfort headboard that uses an active noise control (ANC) system to reduce low-frequency environmental and snoring noises, thus enables the consumers to sleep in a serene environment. The ANC system uses adaptive feedback ANC algorithm with error microphones and loudspeakers mounted on the headboard. MATLAB simulations using the measured transfer functions from the experimental setup are used for designing adaptive algorithm. Real-time experiments using a floating-point digital signal processor demonstrate the designed headboard is effective for reducing snore and other undesired noises.

articleTitle: Residential HDTV distribution system using UWB and IEEE 1394
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: We propose a residential HDTV distribution system that is composed of UWB and IEEE 1394. The proposed system converts multi-channel MPEG TS broadcasting data into IEEE 1394 packets or UWB packets based on IEEE 802.15.3 WPAN. Any distributed UWB packets are again converted into MPEG TS data through a UWB-to-IEEE 1394 bridge. Moreover, this system can also transmit IPTV packets encapsulated with IEEE 1394 packets from a home gateway or home server to a home UWB network.

articleTitle: Download-based home network adapter
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper presents the adapter that connects every household appliance and the home network, which can download communication protocol between an appliance and an adapter. The adapter has two controllers that make the electric current supplied from an appliance smooth, and the appliance can reduce the power supply capacity.

articleTitle: Meaningful scene filtering for TV terminals
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Digital broadcasting has been in progress for user-friendly TV watching environment by personalized broadcasting services. As one of the services, a meaningful scene filtering for TV terminals including a set-top box and a personal video recorder (PVR) is proposed in this paper. Using the proposed filtering, TV viewer can find desired scenes from multiple programs of multiple channels simultaneously. The usefulness of the proposed content filtering is verified with sport video on a broadcasting system with intelligent agent platforms.

articleTitle: An integrated home server for communication, broadcast reception, and home automation
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper presents a home server integrating communication, digital broadcast reception, and home automation applications. The home server has a CPU of high performance, and an MPEG decoder as a PCI slave device, and a MPEG2 TS distributor to convey simultaneously three HDTV channels which may go their way from terrestrial, satellite, and cable tuners to the next destination equipment via Ethernet port and PCI bus. We also present the architecture of MPEG2 TS distributor.

articleTitle: Implementation of a digital convergence platform for future home multimedia appliances
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper describes a digital convergence platform (DCP), which is implemented based on the MPEG-21 multimedia framework. The DCP is a newly proposed solution in this research for the convergence service of future home multimedia environment. The DCP is a common platform designed to have the feature of configurability, via means of S/W, which is needed for the convergence service of diverse digital media. A distributed peer to peer service and transaction model is also a new feature realized in the DCP using the MPEG-21 multimedia framework. A prototype DCP is implemented to verify its functions of multimedia service and transactions. The developed DCPs are networked with IP clustering storage systems for the distributed service of multimedia. Successful streaming services of the MPEG-2/4 video and audio are verified with the implemented test-bed system of the DCP

articleTitle: Noise reduction for interpolations based on pilot-block averaging in DVB-T receivers
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper proposes a noise-reduction method to improve the channel-estimation performance in DVB-T receivers. Pilot-insertion type approximation and pilot-block averaging are employed to reduce noise effect. Computer simulation shows that the proposed method improves the estimation performance by more than 1 dB in terms of the SER after equalization.

articleTitle: Secure service discovery in home networks
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper presents architecture for secure service discovery for use in home networks. We give an overview and rationale of cluster-based home network architecture that bridges different, often vendor specific, network technologies. We show how it integrates security, communication, and service discovery to achieve a secure and trusted way of deploying services in a domestic environment.

articleTitle: Distributed and adaptive multimedia content analysis prototyping framework for consumer electronics
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: The ever-increasing complexity of generic multimedia-content-analysis-based (MCA) solutions, their processing power demanding nature and the need to prototype and assess solutions in a fast and cost-saving manner motivated the development of the Cassandra framework. The combination of state-of-the-art network and grid-computing solutions and recently standardized interfaces facilitated the set-up of this framework, forming the basis for multiple cross-domain and cross-organizational collaborations. It enables distributed computing scenario simulations for, for example, distributed content analysis (DCA) across consumer electronics (CE) in-home networks, but also the rapid development and assessment of complex multi-MCA-algorithm-based applications and system solutions. Furthermore, the framework's modular nature - logical MCA units are wrapped into so-called service units (SU) - ease the split between system-architecture - and algorithmic-related work and additionally facilitate reusability, extensibility and upgradeability of those SUs

articleTitle: Multimedia room bridge adapter for seamless interoperability between heterogeneous home network devices
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper presents a multimedia room bridge adapter (MRBA) system that is designed to manage heterogeneous devices with seamless interoperability and support various services effectively in fully distributed home network

articleTitle: A low power multimedia system based on the microscopic dynamic voltage scaling (DVS)
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper presents a DVS based multimedia system which is designed to effectively reduce the power consumption of multimedia signal processor. The DVS control technique of the system capitalizes the microscopic, i.e., frame-wise, variations of processing requirement for the application of reduced supply voltage and frequency levels. The Xscale processor based DVS system is implemented and performs an MPEG-2 audio/video decoder algorithm for experimental verification of the power saving.

articleTitle: Architecture for interoperability of services between an ACAP receiver and home networked devices
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: As digital convergence of home networking and broadcasting technologies is being accelerated, it is very important to achieve interoperability of not only heterogeneous devices but also their services. This paper presents the architecture for interoperability of data broadcasting and home networking services between an ACAP (advanced common application platform) receiver and home networked devices.

articleTitle: Improved update steps through motion vector correlation analysis for scalable video coding
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Recent breakthroughs in motion-compensated temporal filtering (MCTF) has enabled the realization of scalable video coding (SVC). In this paper, we propose a new scheme to improve the update steps of MCTF by analyzing the correlation of the motion vectors (MVs) of the neighboring blocks as well as the correlation of the derived update MVs in the low-pass frames. Results show that the proposed algorithm improves the visual quality of reconstructed video sequences at different bit rates.
